<reason>A establishes a distinct preventive obligation that prosecuting attackers does not supply, and answers pressure with contemporaneous evidence requirements, targeted interventions, and compliance protections. B lands a significant objection: determining whether precautions were warranted remains contestable, so the safe harbor cannot eliminate defensive moderation. But B overstates this into an assertion that suppression is always cheaper and repeatedly treats existing criminal prohibitions as sufficient answers to platform inaction. A’s closing acknowledges residual risk while preserving the comparative case for bounded responsibility. B never adequately defeats that case, particularly for clear, actionable warnings.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between an attacker’s crime and a platform’s omission breaks B’s “already criminal or lawful gray zone” dilemma. Punishing the attacker does not impose timely platform precautions. B’s reply about the same facts and deeper pockets does not answer that preventive gap.</best_rebuttal>
